phĭlostorgus , a, um, adj., = φιλόστοργος,
I.loving tenderly, affectionate, esp. of the love of parents and children (postAug.): “philostorgus, cujus rei nomen apud Romanos nullum est,” Front. Ep. ad Amic. 1, 6 ; cf. id. ib. ad Verum, 7.—
II. Written PHILOSTERGVS, a Roman surname, Inscr. Grut. 240, 1.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
